newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian governor-general defends ethnic mix.
newsitem.headline: Australian governor-general defends ethnic mix.

text.p: Australian Governor-General Sir William Deane on Monday entered the country's bitter race debate, saying Australia's ethnic diversity fuelled rather than threatened national unity.
Deane, who represents Britain's Queen Elizabeth as head of state, urged Australians to protect multiculturalism, which is under fire from race row politician Pauline Hanson.
"Multiculturalism does not detract from or threaten our national identity or national unity," Deane said in a speech to a conference on cultural and ethnic diversity.

"To the contrary, while recognising and protecting our diversity of backgrounds, cultures and beliefs, it promotes that identity and unity by building upon and adding cohesion to what we are," Deane said.
Deane said multiculturalism -- a policy aimed at tolerance and a melding of cultures -- was in Australia's best interests.
"It is our responsibilities as Australians to protect and maintain it and to observe its standards and dictates," he said.
Australia has been embroiled in a bitter race debate since last September when independent politician Hanson made her maiden speech, claiming the country was being swamped by Asians.
In fact, Asians only make up 4.8 percent of Australia's 18 million population and 40 percent of Australia's annual immigration intake.
The government has slashed the intake to 68,000 from 83,000 since winning power in March 1996, in a battle to bring down high unemployment.
But Hanson has struck a chord with some voters with her anti-immigration and anti-Aboriginal welfare comments.

Her recently formed One Nation Party averages seven to eight percent in opinion polls, ranking it potentially the third political power behind the ruling Liberal-National coalition and the Labor opposition.
However, Hanson's party rallies have been marred by violent and rowdy protests.
